sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 3: Interacting Fields
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 3; §§3.5.3 and 3.6.2–3.6.3, scalar tree amplitude, two-body decay phase space, and differential cross-section normalization.

contents.name: §3.5.3 scalar quartic tree amplitude and isotropic scattering
contents.support: The source gives the constant tree amplitude -lambda and its isotropic formal scattering interpretation; the local corollary derives the exact symmetry factor and SI area units.

contents.name: §§3.6.2–3.6.3 decay and differential cross-section normalization
contents.support: The source motivates the invariant on-shell measure, flux, and coefficient maps; the local proof evaluates the shell integral and radial Jacobian from the declared mathematical suppliers.

contents.name: §3.6 delta-function volume heuristic and lifetime wording
contents.reason: The local phase-space proof evaluates the shell measure directly and the assigned coefficient makes no survival-time claim; adopting the source's delta-four-square volume heuristic or half-life wording would add assumptions outside the proved scope.
contents.support: The chapter's delta-four-square volume heuristic is not used; its sentence calling 1/Gamma the reciprocal half-life is not adopted. This batch makes no exponential survival or half-life claim.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 4: The Dirac Equation
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 4; §§4.3 and 4.7.1–4.7.3, Clifford algebra, Pauli blocks, positive-/negative-frequency spinors, and spinor bilinears.

contents.name: §4.3 Clifford algebra and Pauli-matrix Dirac representations
contents.support: Tong uses the (+---) metric and a chiral basis; the local proof translates to h=-eta, states the Dirac basis explicitly, and rederives every trace identity.

contents.name: §§4.7.1–4.7.3 positive-/negative-frequency spinors and bilinears
contents.support: The source independently treats finite on-shell Dirac spinors; the local argument constructs rank-two spin planes and normalized completeness sums for M>=0 and E>0.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6: Quantum Electrodynamics
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; QED tree diagrams and §6.6 adding a muon species and the e+e- to mu+mu- channel.

contents.name: §6.6 adding muons and the formal pair-production tree channel
contents.support: The source supplies the channel and formal photon-exchange amplitude context; the local theorem derives the full-mass spin trace, angular coefficient, flux normalization, and stated electron-mass-only bound.

contents.name: §6 QED formal tree rules
contents.support: Used as an independent full-text treatment of tree-level QED conventions; no interacting continuum S-matrix or empirical cross section is inferred.

sources.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-posted prepublication draft
sources.locator: Complete 616-page author-hosted book draft; §11 pp. 93–99, §§46–48 pp. 292–302, §59 pp. 351–355, and §64 pp. 383–385.

contents.name: §11 two-body kinematics, invariant phase space, flux, and symmetry factor
contents.support: The book derives the Kallen root, radial Jacobian, dLIPS2 density, CM flux normalization, and factorial correction for identical final particles; the local proof redoes the calculation in the declared h and SI conventions.

contents.name: §§46–48 spin sums, gamma traces, and spin-averaged coefficients
contents.support: The book derives completeness-based trace reduction and the even gamma traces used by the local finite-matrix proof.

contents.name: §59 spinor-QED tree rules and current conservation qualification
contents.support: The book supplies an independent QED tree calculation; it defers the Ward-current proof to a later section, while the local special-case contraction is proved from the spinor equations.

contents.name: §64 minimally coupled Dirac magnetic moment
contents.support: The source independently treats the minimal Dirac magnetic coefficient and later radiative term; this item proves only the exact compact-core square and formal lowest-order g_s=2 coefficient.

contents.name: §64 one-loop form-factor and experimental comparison
contents.reason: The assigned item proves the compact-core differential square and formal minimal tree coefficient only; a radiative form factor and empirical comparison require loop calculations and experimental inputs outside this mathematical claim.
contents.support: The one-loop F2 contribution, high-precision comparison, and empirical anomaly are outside this mathematical item and are not used.
